optimizedContext.value:
# SQLite Graph Store
## Rules
- `SQLiteGraphStore` implements `GraphStore` (semantics per `code-graph:graph-store`); stable backend id `sqlite`; sole built-in backend, selected when no explicit `graphStoreId`. Native DB-module binding deferred until `open()`; safe open/close; execute schema DDL on first use; keep backend schema-version state; `close()` idempotent.
- Persistence rooted at project `configPath`: DB file + WAL/shared-memory companions only under `{configPath}/graph`; scratch under `{configPath}/tmp`; create dirs on demand; scratch artifacts cleaned after success.
- Durably persist file/document/symbol/spec/relation/meta state; atomic mutations; FTS + identity-aware search; bulk indexing + full re-index; structured queries (traversal, references, coverage, impact, hotspots, search, stats). Graph unreadable after backend change → full SQLite re-index = recovery path.
- `recreate()`: discard all `{configPath}/graph` data incl. WAL/SHM companions belonging to same root, rotate storage-generation marker (`graph/storage.epoch` sidecar acceptable), ready for clean rebuild. `open()` exposes current generation to owning provider; rotation makes older open providers detect staleness and reopen.
- Persist node kinds: `File` (incl. source content for symbol snippet extraction), `Symbol`, `Spec`, `Document` (columns `path` PK, `configRelativePath`, `contentHash`, `content`, `workspace`), `Meta`. Persist relations `IMPORTS`, `DEFINES`, `CALLS`, `EXPORTS`, `DEPENDS_ON`, `COVERS_FILE`, `COVERS_SYMBOL`, `EXTENDS`, `IMPLEMENTS`, `OVERRIDES`; single table/per-type layout both OK if observable `GraphStore` query semantics preserved; `COVERS_SYMBOL` entries preserve relation metadata so symbol-level implementation links surface `stale` consistently after reload.
- FTS5: virtual tables `symbol_fts` (`name`,`comment`), `spec_fts` (`title`,`description`,`content`), `document_fts` (`path`,`content`). Keep FTS `MATCH` candidate generation for `searchSymbols()`, `searchSpecs()`, `searchDocuments()`; MUST NOT replace retrieval with plain whole-query `LIKE` filtering. Sanitize + join multi-token queries with `OR`. Expand raw tokens via shared specd/code-aware lexical policy before ranking; supplement FTS candidates with identity-derived hits when tokenization misses strong identity hit.
- Identity-aware ranking via explicit SQL ordering (computed rank columns / `CASE`), not BM25 weights alone. Ordering: exact canonical identity matches rank first (Spec ID, Symbol Name/ID, Document Path); non-exact identity hits ahead of body-only/comment-only/content-only; exact token > prefix token > suffix token > arbitrary substring token; real identity-component match beats substring-only same-field; more expanded identity tokens beats fewer when generic relevance competes; BM25 ranks remaining textual matches after identity preference; generic body term frequency MUST NOT outrank stronger spec-id/symbol-name/document-path match. Non-exact identity includes symbol declared-name equality, spec-id prefix/suffix/substring/component, document canonical/config-relative path prefix/suffix/substring/component. Derive match-aware snippets + 1-based line range from persisted file source or FTS matches. Persisted `File` snippet content SHALL NOT become separate searchable file category in this change.
- Transactions preserve abstract atomic mutation semantics: `upsertFile()`, `removeFile()`, `upsertSpec()`, `removeSpec()` replace/remove file-/spec-local state atomically; bulk commits all-or-nothing for claimed batch; failed transaction leaves previously committed state intact.
- Reference schema upgrade: persist enriched logical-symbol, declaration, member, symbol-space, binding, provenance, coverage, complete construct range, declared-name selection range fields. Structured workspace/surface/name/symbol-space/owner/member-form/exported-name columns indexed for semantic search + selector resolution without parsing or substring-ranking serialized canonical ids; canonical ids remain unique external identities; backend-local integer row keys MAY join physically if provider-visible ids unchanged.
- Dedicated source-file content FTS index, substring-capable trigram tokenization. Candidate queries use shared complete/raw/expanded query plan; honor filters before candidate limits; return indexed content or precise evidence for Code Graph verification; queries shorter than three characters use bounded indexed/SQL fallback per shared Store contract, never every file for application-layer scanning. Batched reverse coverage lookup: set-based predicates over deduplicated file paths + symbol ids, deterministic ordering.
- Persist incremental-hydration state: indexed-input observations, workspace/global latches, VCS-scope evidence, compact unchanged-file facts. One indexing run = one database transaction, set-based relation endpoint validation, bounded prepared/bulk inserts, one commit, one rebuild of all semantic + content FTS indexes. Chunk appends MUST NOT rebuild FTS independently.
- Open sequence: execute current schema definition → verify/record schema version in metadata → prepare FTS structures. Incompatible persisted schema version MAY require destructive rebuild instead of incremental migration; increment schema version exactly once relative to version at implementation start (`5`→`6` absent intervening change); incompatible DB MUST reject ordinary reads; `graph index` rebuilds destructively, rotates `storage.epoch`, completes FTS rebuild before marking ready.
## Constraints
- Infrastructure adapter, not part of abstract graph-store contract.
- `sqlite` stable backend id in multi-backend graph-store registry.
- SQLite file layout, FTS behavior, schema shape, schema-version handling defined here, not `code-graph:graph-store`.
- All SQLite scratch files + persisted artifacts rooted under `configPath`.
- Storage-agnostic use cases + CLI commands MUST NOT depend on this spec unless truly requiring SQLite-specific behavior.
